statement: The dead-man receiver answers. A receiver that is up but not answering is worse than one that is down, because every wrapped job still reports success.
acceptance_cmd: base=$(cat "$HOME/.estate/healthchecks/base" 2>/dev/null || echo http://127.0.0.1:8000/ping); root=${base%/ping}; code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -m 5 -w '%{http_code}' "$root/" 2>/dev/null); echo "receiver $root -> HTTP $code"; [ "$code" = "200" ] || [ "$code" = "302" ]

statement: Every loaded estate job is wrapped in the dead-man switch. The population is every loaded job that has a plist, never a name prefix: filtering on ai./com.chidionyema./com.founder. hid 14 jobs on 2026-08-24, three of them already wrapped.
acceptance_cmd: bare=0; total=0; for l in $(launchctl list 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | awk '{print $3}' | grep -vE '^(com\.apple\.|application\.|0x|com\.valvesoftware\.|homebrew\.)'); do p="$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/$l.plist"; [ -f "$p" ] || continue; total=$((total+1)); /usr/bin/grep -q hc-wrap "$p" || { bare=$((bare+1)); echo "BARE $l"; }; done; echo "$((total-bare))/$total wrapped, $bare bare"; [ "$bare" -eq 0 ]

statement: The receiver does not run inside the failure domain it watches. A monitor on this Mac cannot report that this Mac is dead, and on 2026-08-24 the local container proved it: up 6 hours, unhealthy, answering HTTP 000 while every wrapped job still exited 0.
acceptance_cmd: base=$(cat "$HOME/.estate/healthchecks/base" 2>/dev/null); echo "base=${base:-<unset, defaults to the local container>}"; [ -n "$base" ] && ! echo "$base" | grep -qE '127\.0\.0\.1|localhost|::1'

statement: Something outside the receiver notices when the receiver stops answering. hc-wrap.sh is fail-open by design, which is right for the job and means a dead receiver is silent. Wrapping more jobs multiplies that silence rather than fixing it. Found by session chidionyema-7e, 2026-08-24.
acceptance_cmd: snap="$HOME/dev/code/crew/STATE.md"; [ -f "$snap" ] || { echo 'no estate snapshot on disk'; exit 1; }; grep -iqE 'healthchecks|dead.man|receiver' "$snap" && echo 'the hourly snapshot carries a receiver row' || { echo 'STATE.md has no receiver row -- nothing reports that the monitor is down'; exit 1; }

statement: A job with no ping key configured is not silently unmonitored. hc-wrap.sh guards both pings with [ -n "$PK" ], so a missing key means the job runs, exits 0, and is never watched, which looks identical to a healthy monitored job.
acceptance_cmd: k="$HOME/.estate/healthchecks/ping_key"; if [ -s "$k" ]; then echo "ping key present ($(wc -c < "$k" | tr -d ' ') bytes, value never printed)"; else echo 'no ping key: every wrapped job is silently unmonitored and still exits 0'; exit 1; fi
